assumptions: The February 2027 battery-passport obligation and covered battery categories remain materially as described in the packet, although implementation guidance may continue to change.
The venture has no customer, channel commitment, proprietary data right, or specialist compliance credential beyond what is explicitly evidenced.
A customer can authorize access to relevant records, but supplier cooperation and the authenticity and completeness of upstream evidence cannot be guaranteed by the venture.
The proposed prices, delivery effort, renewal frequency, and contribution margin are hypotheses until demonstrated in paid engagements.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Evidence from at least three paid pilots in one sharply defined battery segment, showing accepted pricing, quantified avoided delay or rework, measured delivery and exception hours, positive contribution margin, sales-cycle and CAC data, and at least one repeat engagement or signed channel/workflow agreement.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Moving evidence verification upstream of supplier or model approval addresses a concrete failure point and is more focused than operating a full passport platform. The insight is useful but not proprietary, and established vendors can add the same checkpoint.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: The statutory deadline, operator accountability, and documented SME implementation difficulty support real urgency and potential loss avoidance. However, there is no evidence that a smaller operator will separately buy this exact acceptance sprint rather than use internal staff, free resources, a consultant, or a broader platform.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Deposits, fixed scope, customer-hosted work, and avoidance of long-lived hosting reduce capital needs and cash-conversion risk. Pricing, acquisition cost, delivery hours, exception burden, repeat frequency, retention, insurance cost, and margin are all unmeasured, while the founder-wealth path requires substantial account scale and delegated delivery.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Covered batteries create an economically relevant EU compliance market, but the proposed beachhead spans several materially different battery categories and all smaller EU operators. The reachable number of underserved operators in a first geography and category is not established.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Platform neutrality and a pre-procurement focus offer positioning room, but the venture owns neither the approval decision nor the supplier relationship and has no secured channel. Siemens, Minespider, public tools, and certifier-platform alliances already cover much of the workflow and can bundle this feature.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful wedge could extend across additional suppliers, models, battery categories, geographies, and eventually other digital-product-passport workflows. Expansion is plausible, but customer-specific delivery and restricted cross-customer data reuse limit compounding and make adjacency capture uncertain.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Customer-specific mappings and exception history may create modest workflow familiarity and switching friction. Open standards, mandatory portability, customer ownership, limits on data reuse, public validation resources, and easy incumbent bundling prevent a strong durable moat as currently structured.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A bounded, platform-neutral, customer-hosted deliverable may be simpler and lower-commitment than buying a full passport system. No measured price, speed, accuracy, trust, or risk-reduction advantage is shown, and a competitor's fixed annual plan includes substantially broader functionality.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The approaching 2027 obligation and still-evolving implementation details create a genuine preparation window and immediate reason to act. Registry and semantic-catalogue immaturity also introduce delivery uncertainty, while established vendors are already active.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Laboratory and import-adviser referrals are logically aligned, and technical outreach does not require a public-facing founder brand. No partner has agreed to refer or co-deliver, acquisition economics are unknown, and scaled certifier-platform partnerships may pre-empt the most credible channels.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data-lineage skills, low initial capital need, and ability to run one bounded pilot support feasibility. Regulatory interpretation, security, professional liability, supplier chasing, domain credibility, and concurrent exception work could exceed a five-hour daily limit before templates and staff are proven.

highest_value_structural_change: Secure a signed co-delivery arrangement with a credible independent battery laboratory or import-compliance adviser that makes the evidence pack a default pre-approval step for one narrowly defined battery category, with explicit referral economics, customer authorization, and bounded responsibility.
main_structural_strength: The offer ties a bounded, deposit-funded deliverable to a specific procurement decision before an incomplete evidence pack can cause costly launch rework, while avoiding the open-ended burden of passport hosting.
primary_score_limiter: The venture lacks a controlled workflow position, differentiated capability, or proven channel, while willingness to pay and fully loaded service economics remain unvalidated against broad incumbent offerings.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Minespider publicly offers an annual small-team plan with unlimited passports and models, evidence storage, audit, validation, and integration for EUR 11,900, while Siemens and a Bureau Veritas-Circulor alliance also cover overlapping upstream work; this materially challenges both differentiation and the proposed standalone pricing.
